sessions.study_goal:
# Write an arguable thesis before drafting the body of the history essay.

Use primary sources as evidence, distinguish an author's claim from your own interpretation, and connect each paragraph back to the thesis. Plan the essay in three stages: outline the argument, draft paragraphs with evidence, then revise the introduction and conclusion.

sources.text:
# History essay draft

For the history essay draft, write an arguable thesis before drafting the body. Use primary sources as evidence, distinguish an author's claim from your own interpretation, and connect each paragraph back to the thesis.

Plan the history essay in three stages: outline the argument, draft paragraphs with evidence, then revise the introduction and conclusion. Keep a bibliography while writing and cite quotations and paraphrases. Check the assignment's required citation style before submitting.

sources.text:
# Python lab

For the Python lab, break the program into small functions with clear inputs and outputs. Implement the core behavior first, then write unit tests covering normal input, empty input, and invalid values. Use pytest to run the tests locally.

Before submitting the Python lab, check file paths and handle missing files with a helpful error. Test the code with a fresh virtual environment and keep dependencies in requirements.txt. Do not hardcode personal file paths or credentials.

sessions.title: Economics reading
sessions.study_goal: Review economics reading material focusing on supply, demand, equilibrium, and price elasticity, sketch curves, identify shifts, and understand their effects.

sources.text:
# Economics reading

For the economics reading, review supply, demand, equilibrium, and price elasticity. Sketch the supply and demand curves, identify which curve shifts in each example, and explain the effect on equilibrium price and quantity.

After each economics section, close the book and summarize the main idea from memory. Compare elastic and inelastic demand using examples, then attempt the end-of-chapter questions. Record unfamiliar terms so they can be reviewed before the next class.
